title: When the Sigil Falls Again
premise: Marguerite Almeida fled her duty as gatekeeper three years ago, when the covenant binding the fae realm to hers was shattered and magic was outlawed in reprisal. A dying courier's map reveals that the sigil sealing the gate is failing, and that the man who broke the covenant—now the city's beloved magistrate—is racing to claim the gate's power for himself. Pursued by his enforcers and guided by a fae exile who remembers what she has spent years trying to forget, Marguerite must reforge the covenant with her own blood and memory before the thirteenth moon turns. In the end she chooses justice over vengeance: she seals the gate anew but leaves it open a crack, so that neither realm can ever again pretend the other does not exist.
about_author: Wren Nakamura is a former archivist who writes fantasy about people who keep things—gates, secrets, promises—that were never meant to be kept alone. She lives between two cities and one coastline, and claims the best plot ideas arrive on trains.

chapters.title: The Courier's Last Breath
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. In the outlaw city of Vessengard, Marguerite sells harmless charms while hiding her true nature as the gate's runaway keeper. A bloodied stranger collapses in her shop and presses a wax-sealed map into her hands, whispering that the sigil is falling and naming the magistrate Corvane as its breaker. Enforcers arrive; she barely escapes through her own hidden craft. Emotional beat: guilt rekindled—the past she buried has found her.

chapters.title: What the Exile Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Sef, a fae exile who guards the map's first waypoint. He recognizes Marguerite as the keeper who abandoned her post and forces her to confront the memory she suppressed: the night the covenant broke, and her sister's role in it. Together they decode the map toward the gate, learning Corvane plans to complete his claim at the thirteenth moon. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance forged from shared shame and sharpening resolve.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons, One Door
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Captured by Corvane's enforcers, Marguerite is brought before the magistrate, who offers her partnership: let him hold the gate, and no one need remember the covenant's original price—including her sister's sacrifice. Offered comfort instead of truth, she refuses, escapes with Sef's aid during a moonlit riot, and races to the gate as the thirteenth moon rises. Emotional beat: climax of choice—she rejects the seduction of forgetting and embraces costly memory.

chapters.title: A Crack of Light
chapters.summary: Shared POV. At the gate, Marguerite reforges the covenant using her own memories as ink, reliving every loss rather than erasing them, while Sef holds the threshold against Corvane's final assault. The sigil remade, Corvane's stolen power fails and he faces the city's reckoning outside any court. Marguerite seals the gate—but deliberately leaves it open a crack, appointing herself its honest keeper. Emotional beat: resolution through acceptance; power bounded by memory, justice beyond law.
